evidence_boundary: This ledger records a source-level semantic review of lessons, worked answers, case studies, exercises, worksheets, rubrics, and lab guides. It verifies named mechanisms against bounded primary or official sources, distinguishes normative course contracts, and does not turn synthetic examples into production measurements.

claims.claim: Let P mean the effect completed and A mean progress was acknowledged. Acknowledging before processing gives a crash window A -> crash -> not P: work is lost. Processing before acknowledging gives P -> crash -> not A: work repeats. Networks cannot reveal whether a lost response preceded or followed commitment, so ambiguity is normal.

claims.claim: A partitioned log usually offers total order only inside one partition. A consumer group assigns each partition to at most one active member of that group, so maximum useful parallelism is bounded by partition count and skew. Global order is expensive and rarely required; per-aggregate version monotonicity often preserves the real invariant.

claims.claim: Directly writing a database and broker creates two authorities with a crash gap. The transactional outbox instead inserts the domain change and immutable event intent in one database transaction. A publisher or CDC connector may repeat delivery, but it cannot silently omit a committed fact while the outbox remains queryable.

claims.claim: Replay is a migration and recovery operation, not simply resetting an offset. Freeze the source range and hashes, select code/schema versions, disable or idempotently gate irreversible effects, isolate capacity, write to a shadow view when possible, compare with authority, then cut over or discard.

claims.claim: A workflow spans multiple local transactions. Its correctness comes from recorded state, valid transitions, stable step identities, retry rules, compensation, and reconciliation—not from pretending the entire sequence is one ACID transaction.
